Overview
Course introduction
The Department of Chemistry provides a vibrant environment for postgraduate study. We foster an interdisciplinary approach to science, cutting across physical and life sciences to explore new chemistry frontiers and delivering fundamental solutions for a sustainable and healthy society.
Modern chemical science has profound impact beyond the traditional discipline boundaries. Realising the transformative power of chemistry at discipline interfaces is central to the scientific advances that are needed to solve some of the most pressing problems of the 21st century in medicine, energy, and environment.
At the heart of these scientific solutions are molecules; how they behave, interact, and form new substances, and this is the domain of chemistry. Our department aims to advance fundamental knowledge through original research and bridge the gap between innovative ideas and application-driven endeavours.
We harness our interdisciplinary skills in four research themes, which go beyond traditional chemistry:
Chemistry of life across scales – a new era of functional biology
Chemical biotechnology – harnessing biological strategies for chemical problems
Chemistry for a sustainable society – safeguarding the earth’s resources
Chemistry for new materials – cooperative molecular solutions for technologies of the future
Recent research projects
Chemical origins of biological systems
Discovery and Engineering of new D-peptidases
Emergent properties of biomolecular condensates
Electrochemical activation of pro-drugs of cancer treatments
Furthermore, all recent publications across the department are available to view.
What you will gain
Access to leading academics, facilities, and research training opportunities
Close links with world-leading partner institutions
A recently established, rapidly growing department with an exciting, world-leading research agenda (Ranked 5th UK REF 2021)
A close-knit and vibrant academic and PGR community
Skills, experience and connections to further your career in chemistry
Who is this programme for?
We welcome applications and inquiries from prospective students with a keen interest in chemistry and its adjacent disciplines and a drive to conduct original and impactful research in this area.
Milestones for PhD and MDRes
The steps below show a 'typical' timetable of a full-time PhD and MD degree programme.
Please note that this is only a guide and students should be aware of local procedures in place which may differ as some faculty's may have shorter time frames.
Students following a part-time research degree programme are expected to follow the basic requirements as set out below, however the timing of the milestones will differ.
Milestone 1: Registration and enrolment (month 1)
Complete formal enrolment
Meet your supervisory team
Agree expectations and ways of working
Submit student supervisor agreement
Milestone 2: Training needs analysis (months 1-3)
Identify development needs with your supervisors
Create a personal training plan
Milestone 3: First progress report (month 3)
Submit your first formal progress report
Review early progress with your supervisory team
Milestone 4: Ongoing progress reports (every 6 months)
Submit progress reports every 6 months after month 3
Reflect on achievements challenges and next steps
Discuss and agree actions with your supervisors
Milestone 5: Ethics approval (months 3-9 typically, if required)
Submit ethics application
Obtain approval before starting data collection
Milestone 6: Upgrade/presentation review for MDRes (months 9-12)
Submit a formal progression report
Undertake an oral assessment (upgrade viva)
Outcome confirms progression to full PhD registration
Milestone 7: Data collection and research (year 2)
Undertake primary research or fieldwork
Continue skills development
Milestone 8: Analysis and thesis writing (year 2 and 3)
Complete analysis
Draft thesis chapters
Refine argument and structure
Milestone 9: Preparing to submit
Submit draft work to supervisors
Confirm readiness for submission via RD1
Milestone 10: Submit exam entry form
Submit your intent for the exam by the deadline
Supervisors nominate examiners
Milestone 11: Thesis submission (months 36-48 typically)
Submit thesis in line with regulations and funder requirements
Milestone 12: Viva examination (up to 3 months post thesis despatch)
Attend viva voce (oral examination)
Respond to questions on your research
Milestone 13: Corrections and final submission (post-viva)
Complete required amendments
Submit final approved thesis
